DLSU · AdRIC · CIVI

Solving Real-World Problems using Computer Vision

The Center for Computational Imaging and Visual Innovations (CIVI) specializes in research projects centered towards solving real-world problems through deep learning solutions trained on visual data. Research projects under CIVI focus on specific goals, particularly (1) data collection, (2) model building and optimization, and (3) application development.

Research, people, and achievements at CIVI.

Conference Presentation

2026 September 14 - 17

Architecture-Aware Structured Pruning for Parameter-Efficient Dense Small-Object Detection

Our BSMSCS student Rafael Subo Yap presented research entitled "Architecture-Aware Structured Pruning for Parameter-Efficient Dense Small-Object Detection" at the 35th International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN), held in Padua, Italy 🇮🇹.

Conference Presentation

2026 September 13 - 17

Multiple Papers Presented in ICIP 2026

Our lab head Arren Matthew Antioquia presented research papers entitled "A Comprehensive Analysis of Lightweight Design Strategies for Camouflaged Crop Detection" and "WiSDet: A Windshield-Guided Few-Shot Framework for Detecting Car Stickers in the Wild" at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP), held in Tampere, Finland 🇫🇮.

Conference Presentation

2026 June 26 - 28

A Systematic Class-Wise Analysis of Challenges and Network Efficacy in Camouflaged Crop Detection

Our BSMSCS student Aaron Gabrielle Dichoso presented research entitled "A Systematic Class-Wise Analysis of Challenges and Network Efficacy in Camouflaged Crop Detection" at the 10th International Conference on Graphics and Signal Processing (ICGSP), held in Okayama, Japan 🇯🇵.

Awards

2026 February 18

Outstanding Thesis Award - Silver Medal

Congratulations to Charles Joseph Hinolan, Mac Andre Javellana, Mari Salvador Lapuz, and Audrea Arjaemi Tabadero on receiving the Outstanding Thesis Award (Silver Medal) for their work, "A Lightweight Computer Vision Model for Camouflaged Crop Detection." This marks CIVI`s second Outstanding Thesis Award in the BSCS program and third award overall. Their research evaluates lightweight object detection strategies, including pruning and knowledge distillation, to balance accuracy and computational efficiency for real-world agricultural applications.

Student Activity

2026 January 27 & 2026 February 17

Focused Research and Manuscript Enhancement (FRAME) Sprint

CIVI held FRAME Sprint – Day 1 at the John Gokongwei Innovation Center, DLSU Laguna Campus, on January 27 and February 16, 2026, guiding BSMSCS and THS-ST3 students in refining research manuscripts and preparing papers for conference and journal submission.

Faculty Engagement

2025 December 11

Game Development Meets Computer Vision

CIVI participated in the DOST-PCIEERD Grand MOA Signing for 2025 Approved Projects on December 11, 2025, at the Philippine Trade Training Center. The event recognized a DOST-PCIEERD-funded project with DLSU GAME Lab exploring synthetic 3D scenes for computer vision.

Our faculty member Dr. John Jethro Virtusio delivered a presentation entitled "Computer Vision in Agriculture" at the 10th DOST-Balik Scientist Program (BSP) Annual Convention, held in the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC).
